title: First Constitution Adopted Since 1975 Revolution
note: Constitution adopted August 14-15, 1991 (sources vary by one day). Core facts confirmed.

title: Kaysone Phomvihane Becomes First President Under New Constitution
note: Kaysone became president under the new constitution in 1991. Confirmed.

title: Death of Kaysone Phomvihane Triggers Leadership Succession
note: Died November 21, 1992. Nouhak became president, Khamtai became LPRP General Secretary. All confirmed.

title: National Assembly Elections Held Under New Constitution
note: Year off by 1. The election was held December 20, 1992, not 1993. Seat count (85) and candidate count (154) match, but the year is wrong.

title: First Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge Opens Over Mekong
note: Opened April 1994 near Vientiane, funded by Australian aid (~A$42 million). All facts confirmed.

title: Sixth LPRP Congress Consolidates Khamtai Siphandon's Power
note: Sixth Congress held in 1996, Khamtai reaffirmed as General Secretary. Confirmed.

title: Laos Admitted as Full Member of ASEAN
note: Admitted July 23, 1997 alongside Myanmar. Confirmed.

title: Asian Financial Crisis Hits Lao Economy
note: Crisis severely affected the kip and Lao economy. Confirmed.

title: Khamtai Siphandon Becomes President
note: Khamtai became president February 24, 1998. Nouhak retired (sources say retired, not resigned due to illness — minor framing difference but not materially wrong). Sisavath Keobounphanh became PM. Confirmed.

title: Pro-Democracy Protests Suppressed in Vientiane
note: October 26, 1999 protest in Vientiane. Student leaders arrested, some jailed for years. Confirmed.

title: Hmong Insurgent Attacks in Vientiane Province
note: Hmong insurgent activity in 2000 is confirmed (attacks in Xieng Khouang Province). Bombings in Vientiane city occurred but attribution to Hmong was disputed by diplomats. The specific claim of attacks 'in Vientiane Province' conflates urban Vientiane bombings with Hmong rural attacks elsewhere.

title: Seventh LPRP Congress Endorses Poverty Reduction Strategy
note: Seventh Congress held in 2001, poverty reduction strategy adopted, Khamtai retained. Confirmed.

title: Constitution Amended to Strengthen National Assembly Role
note: Materially wrong: the 2003 amendment strengthened the judiciary and Supreme Court — it did NOT introduce elected provincial assemblies. Provincial assemblies were introduced in the 2015 revision. The description incorrectly attributes a 2015 change to 2003.

title: Hmong Refugees in Saysomboun Special Zone Exposed by Journalists
note: Journalists documented Hmong civilians hiding in Saysomboun in the early 2000s. Confirmed.

title: Laos Granted Normal Trade Relations Status by United States
note: Congress approved November 2004, signed into law December 2004. POW/MIA cooperation cited. Confirmed.

title: Nam Theun 2 Hydropower Dam Begins Construction
note: Financial close was May 2005 and some preparatory construction preceded it, but major construction (river diversion) did not begin until March 2006. The event year is plausible for early works but overstated.

title: Choummaly Sayasone Elected LPRP General Secretary
note: Eighth Congress 2006, Choummaly elected General Secretary replacing Khamtai. Also became president. Confirmed.

title: Second Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge Opens at Savannakhet
note: Official opening ceremony December 20, 2006 (public opening January 2007). Mukdahan-Savannakhet, funded by Japanese loans. Confirmed.

title: Vang Pao Arrested in United States for Alleged Coup Plot
note: Arrested June 4, 2007 in California. Coup plot charges confirmed. Charges later dropped in 2009. Confirmed.

title: UXO National Regulatory Authority Strengthened
note: NRA with expanded donor support confirmed. ~80 million cluster munitions figure is widely cited. Confirmed.

title: Nam Theun 2 Dam Begins Commercial Power Generation
note: Commercial operations April 2010, exporting ~1,000-1,075 MW to Thailand. Confirmed.

title: Ninth LPRP Congress Reaffirms Choummaly Sayasone
note: Ninth Congress 2011, Choummaly re-elected General Secretary. Confirmed.

title: Laos Joins ASEAN Intergovernmental Human Rights Commission
note: Laos participated in AICHR. Confirmed.

title: Sombath Somphone Forcibly Disappeared in Vientiane
note: Disappeared December 15, 2012 at Vientiane police checkpoint. CCTV footage confirmed state involvement. Confirmed.

title: Laos Accedes to the World Trade Organization
note: Became 158th WTO member on February 2, 2013, after 15 years of negotiations. Confirmed.

title: Xayaburi Dam Construction Proceeds Despite Regional Opposition
note: Construction ongoing in 2013 despite Cambodia/Vietnam objections. Confirmed.

title: Constitution Revised to Modernize Governance Framework
note: 2015 revision expanded articles to 119 and introduced provincial assemblies. Confirmed.

title: Bounnhang Vorachith Becomes LPRP General Secretary
note: Tenth Congress January 2016, Bounnhang elected General Secretary. Thongloun became PM. Confirmed.

title: Obama Becomes First US President to Visit Laos
note: Obama visited September 6-8, 2016 in Vientiane. Pledged $90 million over three years for UXO clearance. First sitting US president to visit Laos. Confirmed.

title: Laos-China Railway Construction Formally Launches
note: Groundbreaking ceremony December 25, 2016. $5.9 billion project (event says $6 billion — close). Belt and Road Initiative confirmed. Confirmed.

title: Laos Hosts ASEAN Chairmanship for First Time
note: Materially wrong: Laos held its FIRST ASEAN chairmanship in 2004-2005, not 2016. The 2016 chairmanship was Laos's SECOND. Claiming 2016 was 'the first time' is incorrect.

title: Xe-Pian Xe-Namnoy Saddle Dam Collapses Killing Dozens
note: Collapsed July 23, 2018 in Attapeu Province. 71 killed, 6,000+ displaced (14,440 per some sources). Confirmed.

title: Severe Flooding Across Central and Southern Laos
note: 2018 monsoon flooding affected 600,000+ people across provinces. Confirmed.

title: Xayaburi Dam Begins Operations on Mekong Mainstream
note: Commercial operations October 2019. Capacity ~1,285-1,295 MW. First major mainstream lower Mekong dam. Confirmed.

title: Don Sahong Dam Begins Operations Near Cambodian Border
note: 260 MW, commissioned 2020, located in Khone Falls area near Cambodian border. Confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Lockdowns Strain Lao Economy
note: COVID-19 border closures and tourism collapse confirmed for 2020. Confirmed.

title: Thongloun Sisoulith Elevated to LPRP General Secretary
note: Eleventh Congress January 15, 2021. Thongloun elected General Secretary and later president. Phankham Viphavanh became PM. Confirmed.

title: Laos-China Railway Opens for Service
note: Opened December 3, 2021. Length is 414 km (event says 422 km — minor error but not material). Confirmed.

title: Lao Kip Loses Half Its Value Amid Debt Crisis
note: Kip depreciated ~68% in 2022 (event says 'over 50%' which is technically accurate). Debt exceeded 100% GDP. Confirmed.

title: Laos Seeks Debt Restructuring from Chinese Creditors
note: Ad hoc deferrals from China rather than formal restructuring confirmed. Confirmed.

title: Sonexay Siphandone Appointed Prime Minister
note: Year off by 1. Sonexay was confirmed as PM on December 30, 2022, not January 2023. He is the son of Khamtai Siphandon — confirmed. But appointment year is wrong.

title: Electricity Export Revenue Falls Short of Debt Service Needs
note: Battery of Southeast Asia strategy falling short of fiscal needs confirmed by multiple sources. Confirmed.

title: Luang Prabang Mekong Dam Construction Accelerates
note: Luang Prabang dam construction ongoing, 1,460 MW project on Mekong mainstream. Confirmed.

title: Government Restructuring and Constitutional Amendments Approved
note: National Assembly approved constitutional amendments and government restructuring on March 20, 2025. 62 articles amended, ministries reduced from 17 to 13. Confirmed.
